newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks slip to close weaker.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks slip to close weaker.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks continued yesterday's negative trend to end softer, still battered by reaction to U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks. * Golds stage rally.
Toronto stocks ended weaker on Thursday after Wednesday's sell-off, but losses were checked by a stunning rally in heavyweight gold issues.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 13.97 points to 6187.46, after closing down 46 points on Wednesday.
"It would have been a lot worse if not for the gain in gold," said International MMS analyst Katherine Beattie.
North American markets digested negative comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday.
Greenspan cautioned that the stock markets might be overvalued and the risk of inflation could prompt a tightening in short-term interest rates.
"I think people are taking Greenspan's comments seriously," Beattie said.
Most of Toronto's 14 sub-indices spiralled downward, led by media, utilities, conglomerates and transportation. The three gainers were golds, up nearly 2.9 percent, base metals and real estate.
Declining issues outnumbered advances 520 to 472. Another 289 traded flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc, Canada's largest publicly traded company, was beaten up by investors after unit Bell Canada said its 1997 profits will fall short of preliminary targets set in March 1995.
Shares fell 2.30 to 66.90 on 4.3 million shares, topping Toronto's most actives.

Bell Canada said late Wednesday that net income will reach C$850 million, down from C$950 million forecast previously. Also, Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it may downgrade the ratings of Bell Canada and its parent.
